short: The time between placing an order and receiving the goods.
seoTitle: Lead Time — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: Lead time is the elapsed time between placing a purchase order and having the goods available to sell. Quoted lead times and actual ones frequently differ.
definition: Lead time is the elapsed time between placing a purchase order and having the goods available to sell. It includes the supplier's processing time, transport and your own receiving and put-away.
bodyHtml:
Why Lead Time matters

Every reorder point depends on lead time, so an optimistic figure produces stockouts no matter how carefully the rest is calculated. Quoted lead times and actual ones frequently differ.

Lead Time formula

Lead time demand = Average daily usage × Lead time in days

This is the core of the reorder point.

How Lead Time works in practice

Record the actual gap between order and availability for each supplier over a few orders and use the observed figure. Track variability too, because an unpredictable supplier costs more in buffer stock than a slow but reliable one.

faq.question: Should I use the supplier's quoted lead time?
faq.answer: Only as a starting point. Use your own measured average once you have a few orders of history.

faq.question: How do I reduce lead time?
faq.answer: A local secondary supplier for critical lines often helps more than negotiating with the primary one.
